task_name: The epic's pull request: found and opened

rubric.result: The objective promises two things and both are in production code. 'Finds the open pull request whose head is a branch': `openOfBranch({ branch, repository })` is declared on the port and implemented in `GhPullRequests`, where `#listArgvFor` now takes the branch verbatim instead of deriving it, and `openOf` delegates with `${LOOP_BRANCH_PREFIX}${issueNumber}` so the `gh pr list` lookup is one decision in one place (grep for `'pr', 'list'` returns 1). 'Opens one there with a title and a body': `open({ repository, branch, title, body })` runs `createArgvFor`'s argv with `safeToRepeat: false`, turns a refusing gh into `EpicPullRequestNotOpened`, an unmatched stdout into `PullRequestNotUnderstood`, and answers `new OpenPullRequest({ number, url })`. Nothing the objective names is missing.

The TDD line names `it('opens_the_pull_request_on_the_epic_branch_and_never_lets_a_creation_be_repeated')` and states four things; the test at gh-pull-requests.test.ts:135 does all four. The argv is written out literally (`['pr','create','--repo','josemerca/ct-loop-sandbox','--head','feat/7','--title','the epic pull request','--body','the epic pull request body']`), never built by calling `createArgvFor`. The answer is asserted against `GhDouble.PULL_REQUEST`, i.e. number `42` out of the url shape `LISTED` captures. The half after the `and` is pinned exactly the way `gh-plan-issues.test.ts:253` pins the same flag: a transient stderr ('error connecting to api.github.com') scripted with a good second answer, then `expect(blipped.calls).toHaveLength(1)`, `expect(blipped.sleeping.slept).toEqual([])` and `EpicPullRequestNotOpened`. The boundary pair the line demands — a stdout with no `/pull/<n>` that must raise rather than invent a number — is the second half of `a_gh_that_refused_to_create_is_told_apart_from_a_gh_that_printed_no_pull_request_url` ('no pull request here\n' -> `PullRequestNotUnderstood`). Names are snake_case, like the rest of that file.

Both Contract blocks are honoured name by name. Port: `openOfBranch({ branch, repository }): Promise<ReviewedPullRequest | null>` and `open({ repository, branch, title, body }): Promise<ReviewedPullRequest>`, parameter names and order as written, each with the file's 'must implement' throw idiom. Adapter: `static readonly CREATED = /\/pull\/(\d+)$/` verbatim, and `createArgvFor` returns `['pr','create','--repo',repository.text,'--head',branch,'--title',title,'--body',body]` verbatim, with `safeToRepeat: false` at the call — what `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` says of `gh issue create` ('The flag is named safeToRepeat. `gh issue create` never gets `true`'). `exceptions.ts` gains `EpicPullRequestNotOpened` as a leaf of `SpecFreezeFailure`, and `PlanCollapse` gains it plus `PullRequestNotRead` and `PullRequestNotUnderstood` with kebab-case codes ('epic-pull-request-not-opened', 'pull-request-not-read', 'pull-request-not-understood'), which is the wire format that document fixes. Two spellings differ from the block without changing it: the brief writes `createArgvFor(asked: {...})` and the diff destructures, exactly as `#listArgvFor` beside it does; and `open`'s unreadable-output cause is `PullRequestNotUnderstood` rather than a leaf of `SpecFreezeFailure` — that is the task's own sentence ('no match is `PullRequestNotUnderstood`, a refusing `gh` is `EpicPullRequestNotOpened`'), and the two causes still reach two distinct codes.

Rows the diff bears on: D-10 (everything new under backend/ is TypeScript) — every changed file is `.ts` and typecheck is green; D-23 (after the freeze the app opens the epic's pull request) — this is the capability the diff adds, and it adds only the opening; D-7 (the app never writes to a pull request after it is opened, no merge anywhere) — the diff adds `pr create` and a `pr list` lookup and nothing that comments, edits or merges; D-11 (a yardstick is imported, never reimplemented) — no yardstick is touched, and `LOOP_BRANCH_PREFIX` still comes from the plugin. Rows D-1, D-6, D-13, D-16, D-18, D-21, D-22, D-25 have no subject in this diff: nothing here stores a phase, names cmux, pastes context into a prompt or opens a gate endpoint. No row is reopened.

Exemplars: `gh-pull-requests.ts` is its own exemplar for the `Gh` idiom and the diff keeps it — static argv builders, failure read as data from `outcome.failed` rather than caught from a throw, typed errors, `OpenPullRequest` frozen at construction; `pull-requests.ts` keeps the 'must implement' port idiom for both new methods; the test follows `gh-plan-issues.test.ts` for the non-repeatable-creation pinning and `coordinating-session-route.ts`'s `Projection` for the new refusals. `conventions/defects.md`, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — no new value that classifies anything is held as a string or a boolean; `branch`, `title` and `body` are payload, and the new refusals enter a `Projection` that raises for an undeclared member instead of a catch-all, which `plan-refusal.test.ts` keeps live; (2) raw map as the return value of logic — none: `open` and `openOfBranch` return `OpenPullRequest`, and `createArgvFor` returns an argv, which is the last step before the wire; (3) two fields that have to agree — no new pair and no sentinel: absence is `null` from `openOfBranch`, typed in the signature, and `open` either answers a pull request or raises; `OpenPullRequest`'s number/url pair predates this diff and is what `gh` itself reports; (4) errors named for what happens — `EpicPullRequestNotOpened` names the outcome, not the module, and inherits from `SpecFreezeFailure`, the family that fits it, not from the root. `conventions/boundaries.md`: the creation is declared not safe to repeat ('The caller declares whether its call is safe to repeat... a creation is not'), the cap and the retry policy still arrive through `Gh`'s constructor, the adapter decides no policy, and the answer's codes are declared explicitly beside their detail rather than derived from a class name. Two things I am declaring rather than reporting, because the plan closed them and the implementer had no other diff to write: `createArgvFor` and `CREATED` are public statics whose only caller today is `open` in the same file (`conventions/simplicity.md`, 'which call breaks without it?'), and the `PullRequestNotRead`/`PullRequestNotUnderstood` mappings answer a request that arrives in a later task — both are written in this task's Contract and prose, and the second is forced anyway by the exhaustiveness test once `PullRequestFailure` stops being excused. Boundaries between layers are respected: the domain gains only the port method and the exception leaf, and the adapter is the only place that knows there is a `gh`.

Three sets of `-` lines touch tests. (1) `plan-refusal.test.ts` drops `!(thrown.prototype instanceof exceptions.PullRequestFailure)` from `startingAPlan` — that makes the surviving exhaustiveness assertion stricter, not weaker, and the task asks for it in as many words ('plan-refusal.test.ts drops PullRequestFailure from the families it excuses'). (2) It removes `a_failure_of_reading_a_pull_request_has_no_refusal_declared_here_because_it_also_travels_down_the_stream_that_is_already_open` — the same sentence covers it ('and the test that they have no refusal, because a request reads one now'), and the removed test asserted the opposite of what the diff now guarantees. (3) The two application test files rename a double's field `open` -> `openAnswer`; no assertion, case or expectation changes, and the task names it ('The last two test files hold a double whose `open` field collides with the new method'). Nothing ended up asserting less without the brief asking for it.

The behaviour the objective promises lives in `backend/src/infrastructure/gh-pull-requests.ts` and `backend/src/domain/ports/pull-requests.ts`, not in the test's scaffolding. `GhDouble` doubles only the external system (the `launch` function and the sleep), which is where testing.md says to cut; the argv the assertions compare against is produced by `createArgvFor`, the number `42` is parsed by `CREATED` out of the url the double printed, and the two error types are raised by `open`. Revert `open`/`openOfBranch` in the adapter and all three new tests fail.

Inside the eight code files, every hunk traces to a sentence of the task: the two port methods, the delegation, `createArgvFor`/`CREATED`/`open`, the exception leaf, the three `PlanCollapse` rows, the two `plan-refusal.test.ts` removals, the three new tests and the double rename. Nothing named in `### Out of scope` is touched: `groom.js`, `slices.js`, the brainstorming skill, the plan events, the dispatcher and the harvest are all untouched, and nothing writes to a pull request after it is opened. The ninth path is the plan itself, an amendment I read line by line. Justified: adding the two application test files to `**Files:**` (the doubles' `open` field genuinely collides with the new port method, and the amendment only adds routes, it removes none); rewriting the `**TDD:**` line so the test name is snake_case (every existing test in `gh-pull-requests.test.ts` is snake_case, and `conventions/testing.md` writes its own example that way) and so the `safeToRepeat: false` half is pinned by an observable transient-failure scenario instead of by the flag itself, which is the stronger assertion and the one the named exemplar `gh-plan-issues.test.ts` uses; the verification commands are unchanged but for a comment. Unjustified and reported below as low: the amendment also deleted the task's `Current state` block, which no sentence of the task asks for.

Three tests are added, all in `gh-pull-requests.test.ts`. Deterministic: no clock, no network, no randomness and no sleep — `gh` is a function that answers from a scripted list and the wait goes to `SleepDouble`, whose `slept` is asserted empty. Isolated: each test builds its own `GhDouble` with its own `calls` and `answers`; nothing is shared, ordered or written to disk. Verifies real behaviour: the assertions are on the literal argv the adapter sent, on the `OpenPullRequest` it parsed out of the url gh printed, and on which exception type each failure cause produced — none of them is on a mock's call count standing in for production logic, and all three fail if the production lines of this diff are reverted. I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` before looking for anything finer: its 'Good Tests' table says a name with 'and' in it should be split, and `opens_the_pull_request_on_the_epic_branch_and_never_lets_a_creation_be_repeated` carries one — but that literal name and its two halves are what the `**TDD:**` line prescribes, so item 2 and that sentence cannot both be satisfied; I declare it here instead of reporting it. The other two-case test, `a_gh_that_refused_to_create_is_told_apart_from_a_gh_that_printed_no_pull_request_url`, is one behaviour: `conventions/testing.md` requires that 'both failure causes of every adapter are told apart in its tests', and it proves one is not an instance of the other.

findings.what: The plan amendment deleted task 4's `Current state` block along with the prose reflow. No sentence of the task asks for it, and the block was still true after the change — `backend/src/domain/ports/pull-requests.ts` line 7 still reads `async openOf({ issueNumber, repository }: {`, since the two new methods were added after it, so `plan-contract.js`'s literality check ('the block "Current state (path)" does NOT exist verbatim in that file') would still have passed. Nothing was disarmed — the same file is still named by the Contract block, which is what ct-step checks against the touched paths — so this is a plan edit that removed accurate context rather than a control routed around. The rest of the amendment (the added test-file routes, the snake_case test names, the transient-failure pinning) is justified by the task.
